title: Within-session grip decrement does not establish incremental mobility prediction: an independent NHANES-cycle test
abstract: A frozen order-aware grip-decrement feature was tested beyond peak grip, bilateral asymmetry, age, sex and BMI for concurrent walking limitation in adults aged 60+. Models were fitted in NHANES 2011–2012 (n=1407) and tested in the separately sampled 2013–2014 cycle (n=1524). Weighted log-loss improvement was 0.0000359 (95% rescaled-PSU bootstrap interval -0.000319 to 0.000351); AUROC fell from 0.750794 to 0.750645. The training coefficient had the opposite hypothesized sign. Effort, pain-free and flexible-baseline checks did not establish benefit. This is a negative result for a specific representation and protocol, with independent-cycle validation rather than cross-platform or prospective clinical validation.
